    Navigation Graph

    A Navigation Graph describes screen flow separately from the UXML hierarchy. UITK Navigation uses Unity Graph Toolkit internally for authoring and compiles each .uinavgraph into a runtime UINavigationAsset.

    Asset lifecycle

    1. Create a graph with Assets > Create > UI Navigation > UI Navigation Graph.
    2. Edit nodes and connections in the Graph Toolkit window.
    3. Save the graph.
    4. The Scripted Importer validates the authoring model and regenerates its runtime asset.
    5. UINavigatorBehaviour reads the compiled asset in Play Mode or a build.

    Graph errors are reported on the authoring asset. A graph needs exactly one Start node, at least one screen node, unique screen IDs, and valid connection counts before it can compile cleanly.

    Nodes

    Node Purpose
    Start Declares the graph's single initial route
    UI Applies View commands and exposes UI-driven outputs
    Portal Handles a global Button, Signal, or Toggle route before the active UI
    Random Chooses one connected branch by relative Weight
    Pivot Reroutes and rotates graph wires without runtime behavior
    Time Scale Sets Time.timeScale and continues the action chain
    Debug Log Writes a Normal, Warning, or Error message to the Console
    Load Scene Starts an asynchronous Single or Additive scene load
    Set Active Loaded Scene Makes an already loaded scene active
    Unload Scene Unloads a loaded scene while protecting the final scene
    Application Quit Quits a build or stops Editor Play Mode

    UI routes

    A UI node can expose these output types:

    Output Source
    UI Button A matching NavButton or UINavigationEvents.RequestButtonSignal(...)
    Signal UINavigationEvents.RequestSignal(...)
    Toggle A matching NavToggle; conditions are On, Off, or Any
    Time Delay Unscaled seconds elapsed while this node is active
    UI View A matching NavElement begins an Animated Show or Hide

    Each connected output targets one UI or Action chain. Portal routes are global and are checked before outputs on the active UI node.

    UI View outputs listen to Animated transition start events. Instant View commands and direct InstantShow() or InstantHide() calls do not trigger them.

    View commands and history

    UI nodes can Show or Hide registered Views on both enter and exit. Every View command can be Animated or Instant. If the same View would be both shown and hidden during one transition, Show wins.

    Normal UI outputs are authored as Push transitions. When the connected Action chain reaches another screen, the previous node enters Back history; a terminal Action chain only executes its Actions. Use Back does not control whether a Push transition is authored—it controls whether a Back request on the active node calls UINavigationService.Back(). Add UIBackInputRouter for Escape, Backspace, and mouse Back/Forward input, or call Back() and Forward() from code. A visible View or topmost popup can consume Back before the graph receives it.

    Use Clear History on a UI node when entering it should discard both Back and Forward stacks, such as after sign-in or returning to a title screen.

    Follow Play Mode

    Enable Tools > UI Navigation > Follow Play Mode In Graph to highlight the active node while the application runs. This is useful when an address matches more than one possible route or an Action chain changes the apparent flow.
